approved: National Sports Tribunal (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2019
Regional Services, Sport, Local Government and Decentralisation
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would create the National Sports Tribunal to resolve sporting disputes in Australia.
The bill would update other laws so they work with the new tribunal, including allowing evidence from the sports anti-doping agency to be used in tribunal hearings.
The bill would let the tribunal handle disputes and decisions that happened before, on, or after the new law starts, and sets a 2-year time limit for applications.
Amends the Australian Sports Anti-Doping Authority Act 2006 to let the ASADA CEO present certain assertions and information at tribunal hearings.
Amends the same Act to allow material obtained under a disclosure notice to be used as evidence in the tribunal.
Makes the new tribunal's provisions apply to disputes and decisions regardless of when they occurred.
The Australian sporting community, sports organisations, and the Australian Sports Anti-Doping Authority.

The National Sports Tribunal (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2019 was introduced as a companion to the National Sports Tribunal Bill 2019, covering transitional arrangements and transferring sports dispute resolution functions to the new tribunal. It amends the Australian Sports Anti-Doping Authority Act 2006, with the changes taking effect before the tribunal's establishment on 1 July 2019.
